column1: # AQL Language Specification: scalar edge cases 3 — strings, atoms, booleans
# String-edge coverage via aql:string-util (the empty string through
# every word, byte-vs-rune semantics on multi-byte text, replace's
# interpolation), the EmptyString/ProperString membership split, Atom
# distinctness, boolean truthiness coercion and connective strictness,
# and the scalar↔String conversion words with their malformed-input
# errors. Complements string.tsv, module-string.tsv and boolean.tsv.
# §1  the empty string through every string word

column3: splitting the EMPTY string yields the empty list, not ['']
the empty needle is contained in everything
a real needle is never in the empty haystack
the empty needle matches at position 0
haystack-last: nothing is found IN the empty string
replace in the empty subject is a no-op
an empty search string inserts once at the front (first-occurrence default)
repeating the empty string stays empty
padding the empty string is all spaces

column1: # §2  byte vs rune — size counts BYTES, split '' walks RUNES

column3: size is the BYTE length: é is two bytes in UTF-8
three CJK runes are nine bytes
split '' walks runes — five of them
multi-byte runes split cleanly, never mid-byte
indexof reports a BYTE offset (h=1 + é=2)
repeat is byte-faithful on multi-byte input
pad pads to a BYTE width: ñ (2 bytes) + 2 spaces
ß has no simple-case uppercase — it survives (no SS expansion)
simple case mapping: no final-sigma ς at the word end

column1: # §3  split / concat round-trips and separator edges

column3: split '' then concat is the identity
split on a separator then concat DROPS the separators
split DROPS empty fields: adjacent separators leave no trace
a lone separator splits to NOTHING (both fields empty, both dropped)
a trailing separator adds no empty field
{scope:'all' count:2} caps at two — here that is all of them
matches are non-overlapping, left to right
empty search with {scope:'all'} inserts at every boundary
no match is a no-op, not an error

column1: # §5  template literals — every scalar kind interpolates, holes nest

column3: Boolean and None render as their literals
an Atom interpolates as its bare name
the empty string interpolates to nothing
a template literal evaluates to an ordinary String
a type literal interpolates as its name

column1: # §6  EmptyString / ProperString — '' is a String but NOT a ProperString

column3: the empty string has its own leaf
one proper operand makes the result proper
a ProperString param REJECTS the empty string
a String param spans both leaves

column1: # §7  atoms — quoted words are data, distinct from equal-looking strings

column3: /q quotes a word into an Atom
an Atom never equals the same-spelling String
cross-family ordering vs a String is rejected (use tcmp)
tcmp still orders them: the Atom band sits below Strings
an Atom key reads the same slot as the string key
…and an Atom-keyed set writes the same slot

column1: # §8  truthiness — which values coerce to false in if / not

column3: NaN is TRUTHY — only exact zero is falsy
double negation normalises any value to a Boolean

column1: # §9  connectives — value semantics, strict operands, coercing xor

column3: a paren operand evaluates BEFORE and sees it: no short-circuit rescue
or returns the right operand when the left is falsy…
…even when the right is falsy too (the LAST falsy wins)
or of none picks the right operand
otherwise falls through ONLY for none — 0 passes
guard is STRICTLY Boolean — no truthiness coercion (contrast if)
xor COERCES truthiness (returns a Boolean, unlike and/or)
two falsy strings xor to false
the derived connectives coerce truthiness too
implies on falsy operands (false → false is true)
all of nothing is vacuously true
and returns the deciding operand — here the falsy none

column1: # §10  scalar ↔ String conversion — round-trips and malformed inputs

column3: underscore separators are allowed in Float strings
the special literals parse from strings
scientific notation parses to a Float
the empty string converts to false
…but ANY other non-false text is true — even 'no'
specials stringify to their parseable literals
